claims.statement: Tesamorelin, marketed as EGRIFTA/EGRIFTA SV/EGRIFTA WR, is FDA-approved solely for the reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adult patients with lipodystrophy; original Egrifta was approved November 10, 2010, with Egrifta SV approved in 2019 and Egrifta WR approved March 25, 2025 as reformulations.

context.population: HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy and excess abdominal fat
context.formulation: EGRIFTA SV / EGRIFTA WR (tesamorelin for injection kit)
context.useCase: FDA-approved indication: reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV lipodystrophy

claims.statement: The FDA label explicitly states EGRIFTA SV is not indicated for weight loss management because it has a weight-neutral effect, and that the effect of tesamorelin-induced visceral fat reduction on cardiovascular outcomes or antiretroviral adherence has not been established.

context.useCase: boundary of approved indication vs. weight-loss/off-label use

reviewFlags: safety-critical labeling claim used to counter popular weight-loss marketing

claims.statement: EGRIFTA SV is contraindicated in patients with disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, active malignancy, known hypersensitivity to tesamorelin or excipients, and in pregnancy; labeled warnings include increased neoplasm risk, elevated IGF-1 requiring monitoring, fluid retention, new-onset or worsening glucose intolerance, hypersensitivity reactions, and increased mortality risk reported with growth hormone in critically ill patients.

context.population: HIV-infected adults being considered for or on tesamorelin therapy

extractedEvidence.quote: Disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis due to hypophysectomy, hypopituitarism, pituitary tumor/surgery, head irradiation or head trauma
Active malignancy. Any preexisting malignancy should be inactive and its treatment complete
Pregnant women because modifying visceral adipose tissue offers no benefit in a pregnant woman and could result in fetal harm

reviewFlags: safety-critical claim - full boxed/major warnings text should be independently re-verified against the current label PDF at accessdata.fda.gov before clinical use

claims.statement: Tesamorelin is a synthetic analogue of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) that stimulates the pituitary to release endogenous growth hormone, in turn increasing IGF-1; its molecular formula is C221H366N72O67S (PubChem CID 16137828).
reviewFlags: mechanism-of-action narrative text from the label CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY section was not independently quoted this pass; confirm against label PDF

claims.statement: In a randomized, placebo-controlled trial in HIV-infected patients with abdominal fat accumulation, 6 months of tesamorelin was associated with a significantly greater reduction in visceral adipose tissue than placebo (treatment difference -42 cm^2, p=.005) and a modest reduction in liver fat (net effect -2.9%, p=.003); the study authors characterized it as a preliminary study.

context.population: HIV-infected patients with abdominal fat accumulation
context.useCase: reduction of visceral adipose tissue and liver fat in HIV lipodystrophy (matches approved indication population)
context.doseText: administered for 6 months in the trial protocol; not a use recommendation

extractedEvidence.quote: Tesamorelin significantly reduced visceral adipose tissue (mean change, –34 cm2 [95% CI, –53 to –15 cm2]

In this preliminary study of HIV-infected patients with abdominal fat accumulation, tesamorelin administered for 6 months was associated with reductions in visceral fat and additionally with modest reductions in liver fat.

reviewFlags: trial dose/duration context must never be presented as a use recommendation
authors themselves label findings 'preliminary'; liver fat effect is described as 'modest'

claims.statement: Vendor and wellness-clinic marketing materials cite a small controlled trial reporting improved verbal memory/executive function and reduced hippocampal volume loss with GHRH therapy in older adults (including some with mild cognitive impairment) as support for tesamorelin's 'cognitive benefits,' but this study population and endpoint are distinct from the FDA-approved HIV-lipodystrophy indication, this session could not independently verify the primary trial text (PubMed/PMC access was blocked by bot-verification pages), and no cognitive-function claim appears anywhere in the FDA label; human evidence for cognitive or general anti-aging benefit in the populations tesamorelin is marketed to online is not established.

conflicts.summary: Wellness/vendor marketing content presents cognitive-benefit and general anti-aging framing for tesamorelin, while the FDA label recognizes only a single narrow indication (HIV lipodystrophy abdominal fat) with an explicit weight-neutral limitation; the cited cognition trial could not be independently verified at the primary-source level this session due to PubMed/PMC bot-verification blocks.
